title: Basic statistics
text: functions can compute confidence intervals based vectors tables (full sample), sometimes get point estimates corresponding sample information. Even though formulas straight forward implement, programmed easiness. cases shown : One-sample Z-test Two-sample Z-test One-sample t-test Two-sample t-test One-sample (\chi^2-test) Two-sample (F-test, ratio variances) variance cases functions also report confidence interval standard deviation.

title: Basic statistics
text: form: \bar{x} \pm z_{\alpha/2} \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} function computing ci_z, arguments x sample mean, sig population standard deviation, n sample size, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_z(x = 80, sig = 15, n = 20, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>    mean lower upper #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1    80  73.4  86.6

title: Basic statistics
text: form: \left(\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2\right) \pm z_{\alpha/2} {\sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2_1}{n_1} + \frac{\sigma^2_2}{n_2}}} function computing ci_z2, arguments x1 mean sample 1, sig1 population 1 standard deviation, n1 sample size 1, x2 mean sample 2, sig2 population 2 standard deviation, n2 sample size 2, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_z2(x1 = 42, sig1 = 8, n1 = 75, x2 = 36, sig2 = 6, n2 = 50, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   mean_diff lower upper #>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1         6  3.54  8.46

title: Basic statistics
text: form: \bar{x} \pm t_{\alpha/2,v} \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} function computing ci_t, arguments x sample mean, s sample standard deviation, n sample size, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_t(x = 80, s = 15, n = 20, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>    mean    df lower upper #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1    80    19  73.0  87.0

title: Basic statistics
text: general form: \left(\bar{x}_1-\bar{x}_2\right) \pm t_{\alpha/2,v} {\sqrt{\frac{s^2_1}{n_1} + \frac{s^2_2}{n_2}}} function computing ci_t2, arguments x1 mean sample 1, s1 sample 1 standard deviation, n1 sample size 1, x2 mean sample 2, s2 sample 2 standard deviation, n2 sample size 2, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_t2(x1 = 42, s1 = 8, n1 = 75, x2 = 36, s2 = 6, n2 = 50, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   mean_diff    df lower upper #>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1         6  121.  3.52  8.48

title: Basic statistics
text: form: \frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_{\alpha/2,v}} < \sigma^2 < \frac{(n-1)s^2}{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2,v}} function computing ci_chisq, arguments s sample standard deviation, n sample size, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_chisq(s = 0.535, n = 10, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   stat  value    df lower upper #>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 sd     0.54     9  0.37  0.98 #> 2 var    0.29     9  0.14  0.95

title: Basic statistics
text: form: \frac{s^2_1}{s^2_2} \frac{1}{F_{\alpha/2(v_1,v_2)}} < \frac{\sigma^2_1}{\sigma^2_2} < \frac{s^2_1}{s^2_2} F_{\alpha/2(v_2,v_1)} function computing ci_F, arguments s1 sample 1 standard deviation, n1 sample size 1, s2 sample 2 standard deviation, n2 sample size 2, conf.level desired confidence level:
code: ci_F(s1 = 3.1, n1 = 15, s2 = 0.8, n2 = 12, conf.level = 0.95) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   stat  ratio   df1   df2 lower upper #>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 sd     3.88    14    11  2.11  6.82 #> 2 var   15.0     14    11  4.47 46.5

title: Directional statistics
text: main statistics describe circular data mean direction (\bar{\theta}), mean resultant length (\bar{R}), circular variance (s_0^2). mean resultant length (\bar{R}) ranges 0 1, closer 1 concentrated data closer 0 dispersed data. circular variance (s_0^2) complement mean resultant length (\bar{R}) interpretation opposite, closer 1 variation data. function dir_stats_circ used obtain basic statistics circular data. arguments x vector angular measurements degrees, dir switch indicate data directional (1) non-directional (0), conf.level determine desired confidence level. result shows statistics mentioned , plus concentration parameter kappa (k), general width cone confidence. concentration parameter (k) another measure dispersion, higher concentrated (less dispersed) data, likely preferred mean direction. first example shows set directional data, second example shows set non-directional data.

title: Directional statistics
text: draw planes (great circles) need get coordinates points stereonet, can obtained GreatCircleD function. takes strike (right-hand rule) dip outputs data frame coordinates plotting. planes can added stereonet geom_path. function works 1 plane time, one plane needed can used map2 list_rbind get coordinates planes single data frame.
code: strike = 240 dip = 30 plane <- GreatCircleD(strike, dip)  ggstereo() +   geom_path(aes(xp, yp), plane, col = 'steelblue') set.seed(4101) strike <- runif(min = 30, max = 80, n = 10) dip <- runif(min = 40, max = 60, n = 10) planes <- map2(strike, dip, ~ GreatCircleD(.x, .y)) |>   list_rbind(names_to = "plane_id")  ggstereo() +   geom_path(aes(xp, yp, group = plane_id), planes, col = 'steelblue')

title: Directional statistics
text: extra functions help dealing directional data, used examples. d2s: Converts dip direction strike direction. s2d: Converts strike direction dip direction. rads: Converts degrees radians. degs: Converts radians degrees. StCoordLineD: Converts trend plunge stereonet coordinates. GreatCircleD: Converts strike dip stereonet coordinates great circles. SmallCircleD: Converts trend plunge respective angle stereonet coordinates small circles. SphToCartD: Converts spherical coordinates Cartesian coordinates (unit vectors). CartToSphD: Converts Cartesian coordinates (unit vectors) spherical coordinates. Pole: Returns either strike dip plane given pole, trend plunge pole given plane (right-hand rule convention), input data must radians.

title: Non-linear and self-starting functions
text: GMisc package provides collection non-linear model functions together self-starting routines nls() (base R) drc::drm(). Self- starters automatically derive sensible initial parameter values data, removing need supply starting values manually reducing risk convergence failures. model available three forms: *.fun() — bare mathematical function. SS*() — selfStart object use nls(). DRC*() — drcMean object use drc::drm().

title: Non-linear and self-starting functions
text: Chapman-Richards model describes sigmoidal growth towards upper asymptote : y = \left(1 - e^{-bx}\right)^c Fit nls() Fit drc::drm() Plot  exponential variogram widely used geostatistics model spatial autocorrelation. approaches sill asymptotically: \gamma(x) = \text{nug} + \text{psill}\left(1 - e^{-x / \text{range}}\right) Fit nls() Fit drc::drm() Plot  Modified Kostiakov model describes infiltration rate power-law decay additive constant representing steady-state rate f_c: y = \alpha\, x^{\beta} + f_c Fit nls() Fit drc::drm() Plot
code: set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 60) y <- chaprich.fun(x, a = 10, b = 0.5, c = 2) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.25) df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mod_nls <- nls(y ~ SSchaprich(x, a, b, c), data = df) summary(mod_nls) #>  #> Formula: y ~ SSchaprich(x, a, b, c) #>  #> Parameters: #>   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> a 10.06996    0.10643   94.62   <2e-16 *** #> b  0.45860    0.02496   18.38   <2e-16 *** #> c  1.77995    0.11407   15.60   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.2832 on 57 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 5  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 2.883e-07 mod_drc <- drm(y ~ x, data = df, fct = DRCchaprich()) summary(mod_drc) #>  #> Model fitted: Chapman-Richards growth model #>  #> Parameter estimates: #>  #>                Estimate Std. Error t-value   p-value     #> a:(Intercept) 10.069934   0.105530  95.422 < 2.2e-16 *** #> b:(Intercept)  0.458611   0.024683  18.580 < 2.2e-16 *** #> c:(Intercept)  1.779977   0.113123  15.735 < 2.2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: #>  #>  0.2832407 (57 degrees of freedom) df$fit_nls <- predict(mod_nls) df$fit_drc <- predict(mod_drc)  ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit_nls, colour = "nls"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(     aes(y = fit_drc, colour = "drc"),     linewidth = 1,     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(nls = "steelblue", drc = "tomato")) +   labs(     title = "Chapman-Richards growth model",     x = "x",     y = "y",     colour = "Fit"   ) +   theme_minimal() set.seed(7) x <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 60) y <- varexp.fun(x, nug = 0.1, psill = 0.9, range = 20) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.03) df2 <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mod_nls2 <- nls(y ~ SSvarexp(x, nug, psill, range), data = df2) summary(mod_nls2) #>  #> Formula: y ~ SSvarexp(x, nug, psill, range) #>  #> Parameters: #>       Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> nug    0.09419    0.01697   5.551 7.71e-07 *** #> psill  0.90220    0.01624  55.569  < 2e-16 *** #> range 18.76848    0.72081  26.038  < 2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.02931 on 57 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 4  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.691e-07 mod_drc2 <- drm(y ~ x, data = df2, fct = DRCvarexp()) summary(mod_drc2) #>  #> Model fitted: Exponential variogram model #>  #> Parameter estimates: #>  #>                    Estimate Std. Error t-value   p-value     #> nug:(Intercept)    0.094185   0.016996  5.5417 7.992e-07 *** #> psill:(Intercept)  0.902198   0.016245 55.5360 < 2.2e-16 *** #> range:(Intercept) 18.768462   0.723650 25.9358 < 2.2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: #>  #>  0.02931391 (57 degrees of freedom) df2$fit_nls <- predict(mod_nls2) df2$fit_drc <- predict(mod_drc2)  ggplot(df2, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit_nls, colour = "nls"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(     aes(y = fit_drc, colour = "drc"),     linewidth = 1,     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(nls = "steelblue", drc = "tomato")) +   labs(     title = "Exponential variogram model",     x = "Lag distance",     y = "Semivariance",     colour = "Fit"   ) +   theme_minimal() set.seed(99) x <- seq(0.5, 40, length.out = 60) y <- kostmod.fun(x, alfa = 0.5, beta = -0.6, fc = 0.05) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.02) df3 <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mod_nls3 <- nls(y ~ SSkostmod(x, alfa, beta, fc), data = df3) summary(mod_nls3) #>  #> Formula: y ~ SSkostmod(x, alfa, beta, fc) #>  #> Parameters: #>      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> alfa  0.51203    0.01563  32.768  < 2e-16 *** #> beta -0.59698    0.03182 -18.764  < 2e-16 *** #> fc    0.04094    0.01089   3.758 0.000405 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.01957 on 57 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 4  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.916e-06 mod_drc3 <- drm(y ~ x, data = df3, fct = DRCkostmod()) summary(mod_drc3) #>  #> Model fitted: Modified Kostiakov infiltration model #>  #> Parameter estimates: #>  #>                   Estimate Std. Error  t-value   p-value     #> alfa:(Intercept)  0.512022   0.015606  32.8097 < 2.2e-16 *** #> beta:(Intercept) -0.596995   0.031731 -18.8141 < 2.2e-16 *** #> fc:(Intercept)    0.040941   0.010866   3.7676 0.0003927 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: #>  #>  0.01956542 (57 degrees of freedom) df3$fit_nls <- predict(mod_nls3) df3$fit_drc <- predict(mod_drc3)  ggplot(df3, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit_nls, colour = "nls"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(     aes(y = fit_drc, colour = "drc"),     linewidth = 1,     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(nls = "steelblue", drc = "tomato")) +   labs(     title = "Modified Kostiakov infiltration model",     x = "Time",     y = "Infiltration rate",     colour = "Fit"   ) +   theme_minimal()

Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> alfa  0.51203    0.01563  32.768  < 2e-16 *** #> beta -0.59698    0.03182 -18.764  < 2e-16 *** #> fc    0.04094    0.01089   3.758 0.000405 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.01957 on 57 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 4  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.916e-06 mod_drc3 <- drm(y ~ x, data = df3, fct = DRCkostmod()) summary(mod_drc3) #>  #> Model fitted: Modified Kostiakov infiltration model #>  #> Parameter estimates: #>  #>                   Estimate Std. Error  t-value   p-value     #> alfa:(Intercept)  0.512022   0.015606  32.8097 < 2.2e-16 *** #> beta:(Intercept) -0.596995   0.031731 -18.8141 < 2.2e-16 *** #> fc:(Intercept)    0.040941   0.010866   3.7676 0.0003927 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: #>  #>  0.01956542 (57 degrees of freedom) df3$fit_nls <- predict(mod_nls3) df3$fit_drc <- predict(mod_drc3)  ggplot(df3, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit_nls, colour = "nls"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(     aes(y = fit_drc, colour = "drc"),     linewidth = 1,     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(nls = "steelblue", drc = "tomato")) +   labs(     title = "Modified Kostiakov infiltration model",     x = "Time",     y = "Infiltration rate",     colour = "Fit"   ) +   theme_minimal()

text: idea provide function solves bearing capacity equation different types footings, giving result ultimate (q_u) allowable bearing capacity (q_a): q_u = 0.5 \ B \gamma N_\gamma s_\gamma d_\gamma + D \gamma \left(N_q-1\right) s_q d_q + c N_c s_c d_c q_a = \frac{q_u}{FS} B width meters, D embedment depth meters, FS desired factor safety, c cohesion kPa (referred tau0 function), \gamma unit weight kN/m^3, rest parameters correction factors dependent input values, internal friction angle \phi, type footing (“strip”, “square”, “rectangular”,“circular”), depth water level. function solves equation bearing_capacity, mentioned arguments specifying wet/moist unit weight, saturated unit weight respective use. function outputs table q_u q_a graph results. B D parameters can vectors multiple cases comparisons single values single case estimate. FS = 1 allowable ultimate bearing capacities (q_a = q_u). Different scenarios can analyzed: total stress analysis (TSA) cohesive soil (plastic silts clays) set friction angle equal zero (phi = 0) cohesion equal undrained shear strength (tau0 = Su). effective stress analysis (ESA) cohesive soil use effective friction angle (\phi') effective cohesion (c'). coarse-grained soil (gravels, sands, non-plastic silts) usually TSA = ESA, friction angle cohesion used, material -cohesion set cohesion equal zero (tau0 = 0) Also different methods can used calculate bearing capacity factors (N_\gamma, N_q, N_c), “Vesic” (default), “Terzaghi”, “Meyerhof”, “Hansen”, “Michalowski” “Davis & Booker”. title: Bearing capacity — bearing_capacity
text: B footing's width diameter D footing's embedment depth Lf Length factor footing gamma.h wet/moist unit weight soil gamma.s saturated unit weight soil tau0 soil's cohesion (\(c, \tau_0\)) undrained shear strength (\(s_u\)) phi soil's friction angle (\(\phi\)) (degrees) wl depth water level ground surface FS Factor Safety use calculation \(q_a\) footing Type footing calculate bearing capacity: "square" (default), "strip", "rectangular", "circular" method method use calculate bearing capacity factor \(N_\gamma\): "Vesic" (default), "Terzaghi", "Meyerhof", "Hansen", "Michalowski" "Davis & Booker" case case calculate bearing capacity: "general" (default) "local" metric Logical. TRUE (default) function assume SI units (kN/m3 unit weight, kPa strength parameters, meters dimensions). FALSE, function assume imperial units (pcf unit weight, psf strength parameters, feet dimensions).

title: Bearing capacity — bearing_capacity
text: list three elements: "qu" data frame calculated ultimate bearing capacity combination B D, "qa" data frame calculated allowable bearing capacity combination B D, "Plot" ggplot object showing relationship D qa different values B.

title: Bearing capacity — bearing_capacity
text: B D parameters can vectors multiple cases comparisons single values single case estimates. FS = 1 \(q_a = q_u\). total stress analysis (TSA) cohesive soil (plastic silts clays) set friction angle equal zero (\(\phi = 0\)) cohesion equal undrained shear strength (\(\tau_0 = s_u\)). effective stress analysis (ESA) cohesive soil use effective friction angle effective cohesion. coarse-grained soil (gravels, sands, non-plastic silts) usually TSA = ESA, friction angle cohesion used, material -cohesion set cohesion equal zero (\(\tau_0 = 0\)) general bearing capacity calculated using following equation: $$q_u = \tau_0 N_c s_c d_c + \gamma D \left(N_q - 1\right) s_q d_q + 0.5 B * N_\gamma \gamma s_\gamma d_\gamma$$ : \(N_c\), \(N_q\), \(N_\gamma\) bearing capacity factors, functions soil's friction angle (\(\phi\)) method used calculate , \(s_c\), \(s_q\), \(s_\gamma\) shape factors, depend footing type dimensions, \(d_c\), \(d_q\), \(d_\gamma\) depth factors, depend footing's embedment depth water level, \(\gamma\) unit weight soil, can either wet/moist unit weight (\(\gamma_h\)) bouyant unit weight (\(\gamma_b = \gamma_s - 9.807\)), depending depth water level relative footing. TSA, equation simplifies : $$q_u = s_u N_c s_c d_c$$ : \(\tau_0 = s_u\) undrained shear strength soil, \(N_c\) 5.7 "Terzaghi" 5.14 others. ESA, equation simplifies : $$q_u = \gamma D \left(N_q - 1\right) s_q d_q + 0.5 B * N_\gamma \gamma s_\gamma d_\gamma$$ allowable bearing capacity (\(q_a\)) calculated dividing ultimate bearing capacity (\(q_u\)) Factor Safety (\(FS\)): $$q_a = \frac{q_u}{FS} + \gamma D$$

title: Test for common axis direction (axial) — dir_aov_spher_ax
text: Tests whether two groups 3-D orientations share common principal polar axis. dominant fabric type—cluster (point) girdle—determined pooled PGR indices: point index dominates principal eigenvector (V1) tested; girdle index dominates polar eigenvector (V3) tested. pooled data essentially random formal test performed. null hypothesis rejected pooled axis confidence cone overlaid stereonet. Per-group axes confidence cones always shown distinct colours.

title: Test for common axis direction (axial) — dir_aov_spher_ax

title: Test for common axis direction (axial) — dir_aov_spher_ax
text: trd Numeric vector trend values degrees, unquoted column name data supplied. lines: trend lineation. planes: dip direction strike depending type. plg Numeric vector plunge values degrees, unquoted column name data supplied. lines: plunge. planes: dip angle. grp vector (factor character) group labels, unquoted column name data supplied. Must length trd plg. data data frame (tibble) containing columns referenced trd, plg, grp. Default NULL (use vectors directly). conf.level Numeric. Confidence level per-group pooled axis confidence cones. Default 0.95. type Character. interpret input orientations: "line" (default) Trend plunge lineation. "dir" Dip direction dip angle plane (pole used internally). "strike" Strike (right-hand rule) dip angle plane (pole used internally).

title: Test for common axis direction (axial) — dir_aov_spher_ax
text: named list whose components depend pooled fabric type: PGR Tibble pooled fabric indices: P (point), G (girdle), R (random), B (= 1 − R). statement Character string summarising test conclusion. One : "Samples come distribution common principal/polar axis", "Principal/Polar axis differs samples", "Pooled data follows random distribution" (R dominates). axial_g Tibble per-group axis statistics: group label grp, sample size n, trend trd, plunge plg, confidence cone half-width cone (degrees), concentration parameter kappa, eigenvalue lambda, normalised eigenvalue S. Present data random. axial_res Tibble test statistic Nr, degrees freedom df, p-value p.value. null hypothesis rejected, also includes pooled axis trend trd, plunge plg, confidence cone cone, kappa, sample size N, lambda, S. Present data random. pgrplot ggtern Point–Girdle–Random ternary diagram. Present null hypothesis rejected. stereoplot ggplot equal-area stereonet showing data points per group, per-group axes (coloured squares) confidence cones, —null rejected—pooled axis confidence cone (red principal, blue polar axis).

title: Test for common axis direction (axial) — dir_aov_spher_ax

title: Circular (directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_circ
text: Computes descriptive statistics sample angular measurements (azimuths orientations) using circular statistics. Optionally pulls data column data frame. Handles vectorial data (azimuths, 0°–360°) axial data (strikes lineations, 0°–180°) via dir argument, returns mean direction, resultant length, circular variance, circular standard deviation, circular dispersion, concentration parameter, confidence cone mean direction.

title: Circular (directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_circ
text: x Numeric vector angles degrees, unquoted column name data supplied. data data frame (tibble) containing column referenced x. Default NULL (use x directly vector). dir Integer. Data type: 1 vectorial data (full 360° range, default); 0 axial data (180° range, e.g. strike foliation— angles doubled internally mean halved back). conf.level Numeric. Confidence level mean-direction cone confidence. Default 0.95.

title: Circular (directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_circ
text: one-row data frame following columns: theta.hat Mean direction degrees (0°–360°). N Sample size. R Length resultant vector. Rbar Mean resultant length (R / N); ranges 0 (uniform) 1 (perfectly concentrated). circ.var Circular variance (1 − Rbar). circ.sd Circular standard deviation. circ.disp Circular dispersion. kappa Estimated concentration parameter von Mises distribution. cone Half-width conf.level confidence cone around mean direction (degrees).

title: Spherical (3-D directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_spher
text: Computes descriptive statistics sample 3-D orientations (lines planes) using spherical statistics. function calculates mean resultant vector, concentration parameter, confidence cone mean direction, performs eigenvalue / eigenvector decomposition orientation matrix, estimates distribution parameters Watson bipolar, Watson girdle, Bingham distributions, returns several diagnostic plots (stereonet, eigenvalue ratio plot, PGR ternary diagram).

title: Spherical (3-D directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_spher
code: dir_stats_spher(   trd,   plg,   data = NULL,   conf.level = 0.95,   type = c("line", "dir", "strike"),   plot = c("all", "eig", "mean") )

title: Spherical (3-D directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_spher
text: trd Numeric vector trend values degrees, unquoted column name data supplied. lines: trend lineation. planes: dip direction strike depending type. plg Numeric vector plunge values degrees, unquoted column name data supplied. lines: plunge lineation. planes: dip angle. data data frame (tibble) containing columns referenced trd plg. Default NULL (use vectors directly). conf.level Numeric. Confidence level mean-direction eigenvector confidence cones/ellipses. Default 0.95. type Character. interpret input orientations: "line" (default) Trend plunge lineation. "dir" Dip direction dip angle plane (converted internally pole). "strike" Strike (right-hand rule) dip angle plane (converted internally pole). plot Character. stereonet include output: "" (default) Data points, mean vector confidence cone (gold), three eigenvectors confidence cones (red, green, blue). "eig" Data points eigenvectors confidence cones . "mean" Data points mean vector confidence cone .

title: Spherical (3-D directional) descriptive statistics — dir_stats_spher
text: named list following components: eigen_values 1 × 3 matrix normalised eigenvalues \(S_1 \ge S_2 \ge S_3\) orientation matrix. eigen_vectors 3 × 3 data frame eigenvectors (direction cosines), columns V1–V3. orientation_matrix 3 × 3 orientation (scatter) matrix. trend_plunge 2 × 3 matrix trend (row 1) plunge (row 2) eigenvector degrees. dir_dip 2 × 3 matrix dip direction (row 1) dip (row 2) eigenvector degrees. vector_stats Tibble mean direction statistics: trd, plg, strike, dir, dip, resultant length R, mean resultant length Rbar, concentration parameter kappa, confidence cone half-width cone (degrees), sample size N. axis_stats_watson Tibble confidence cone half-widths eigenvector (V1_cone, V2_cone, V3_cone) estimated concentration parameters Watson bipolar (kappa_bipolar) Watson girdle (kappa_girdle) distributions. axis_stats_aniso Data frame (3 × 3) Bingham κ values Watson confidence ellipse semi-axes (degrees) eigenvector. PointGirdleRandom Tibble fabric indices: P (point/cluster), G (girdle), R (random), B (= 1 − R), eigenvalue ratios \(S_1/S_2\), \(S_1/S_3\), \(S_2/S_3\), log-ratios r1 r2, Woodcock's shape K strength C parameters, intensity index , distance index D. eigenplot ggplot object: log-ratio eigenvalue plot (\(\ln(S_2/S_3)\) vs \(\ln(S_1/S_2)\)) K-lines C-isolines. pgrplot ggtern object: Point–Girdle–Random ternary diagram. stereoplot ggplot equal-area stereonet according plot argument.

title: First-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly1.fun
text: x numeric vector non-zero positive values (e.g., time, distance). coefficient \(1/x\) term linearised form. Controls initial rise curve near origin. b coefficient \(x\) term denominator. reciprocal \(1/b\) gives asymptote response \(x \\infty\).

title: First-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly1.fun
text: model defined : $$y = \frac{x}{+ b x}$$ coefficient \(1/x\) term linearised form (controls initial rise near origin) b coefficient linear term denominator. reciprocal \(1/b\) gives asymptote \(x \\infty\). curve passes origin approaches asymptote \(1/b\) \(x \\infty\).

title: First-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly1.fun
code: x <- seq(1, 20, length.out = 50) y <- invpoly1.fun(x, a = 2, b = 0.5) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.05) df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mod = nls(y ~ SSinvpoly1(x, a, b), data = df) summary(mod) #>  #> Formula: y ~ SSinvpoly1(x, a, b) #>  #> Parameters: #>   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> a 2.018758   0.065033   31.04   <2e-16 *** #> b 0.500286   0.006379   78.43   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.04561 on 48 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 3  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 5.63e-08 #>  plot(x, y, cex = 0.8) lines(x, predict(mod), col = 'blue')   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ mod = drc::drm(y ~ x, data = df, fct = DRCinvpoly1()) summary(mod) plot(mod, log = "") } # }

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
text: functions provide Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model equation (invpoly2.fun()), well self-starters nls() (SSinvpoly2()) drc::drm() functions (DRCinvpoly2()).

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
code: invpoly2.fun(x, a, b, c)  SSinvpoly2(x, a, b, c)  DRCinvpoly2()

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
text: x numeric vector non-zero positive values (e.g., dose, time). coefficient \(1/x\) term linearised form. Controls initial rise curve near origin. b coefficient linear term denominator. Along c, determines location height response peak. c coefficient quadratic term denominator. positive value causes curve decline reaching maximum, producing unimodal response.

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
text: invpoly2.fun() SSinvpoly2() return numeric value, DRCinvpoly2() returns list containing nonlinear function self starter function.

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
text: model defined : $$y = \frac{x}{+ b x + c x^2}$$ controls initial rise near origin, b linear term denominator, c quadratic term. positive c causes curve reach maximum subsequently decline, producing unimodal response. Unlike first-order model SSinvpoly1(), quadratic term denominator allows curve reach maximum subsequently decline, making suitable unimodal dose-response relationships.

title: Second-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly2.fun
code: x <- seq(1, 20, length.out = 50) y <- invpoly2.fun(x, a = 1, b = 0.5, c = 0.02) + rnorm(50, sd = 0.05) df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mod = nls(y ~ SSinvpoly2(x, a, b, c), data = df) summary(mod) #>  #> Formula: y ~ SSinvpoly2(x, a, b, c) #>  #> Parameters: #>   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> a 0.886425   0.073827   12.01 6.36e-16 *** #> b 0.527991   0.025684   20.56  < 2e-16 *** #> c 0.017986   0.001615   11.14 8.79e-15 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.05142 on 47 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 2  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 4.586e-06 #>  plot(x, y, cex = 0.8) lines(x, predict(mod), col = 'blue')   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ mod = drc::drm(y ~ x, data = df, fct = DRCinvpoly2()) summary(mod) plot(mod, log = "") } # }

title: Third-Order Inverse Polynomial Model — invpoly3.fun

Along c d, determines shape location peaks troughs response. c coefficient quadratic term denominator. Contributes curvature can produce unimodal response. d coefficient cubic term denominator. Allows additional inflection points, enabling bimodal complex response shapes.

title: Exponential Variogram Model — varexp.fun
code: varexp.fun(x, nug, psill, range)  SSvarexp(x, nug, psill, range)  DRCvarexp()

title: Exponential Variogram Model — varexp.fun
text: x numeric vector non-negative lag distances. nug nugget: semivariance zero lag distance (intercept). psill partial sill: difference sill (total variance) nugget. range range parameter controlling rate increase. practical range ~95 percent sill reached approximately \(3 \times \text{range}\).

title: Exponential Variogram Model — varexp.fun
text: varexp.fun() SSvarexp() return numeric value, DRCvarexp() returns list containing nonlinear function self starter function.

title: Exponential Variogram Model — varexp.fun
text: model defined : $$y = \text{nug} + \text{psill} \left(1 - e^{-x / \text{range}}\right)$$ nug nugget (semivariance zero lag), psill partial sill (difference sill nugget), range controls rate increase. practical range ~95 percent sill reached approximately \(3 \times \text{range}\). standard exponential variogram model commonly used geostatistics describe spatial autocorrelation. Unlike spherical model, approaches sill asymptotically.

title: Gaussian Variogram Model — vargauss.fun
text: model defined : $$y = \text{nug} + \text{psill} \left(1 - e^{-(x / \text{range})^2}\right)$$ nug nugget (semivariance zero lag), psill partial sill, range controls rate increase. practical range ~95 percent sill reached approximately \(\sqrt{3} \times \text{range}\). Gaussian model smooth, parabolic behaviour near origin compared concave-exponential. Gaussian variogram model commonly used geostatistics describe spatial autocorrelation smooth, parabolic behaviour near origin. Like exponential model, approaches sill asymptotically, S-shaped rise compared concave-exponential curve.

title: Spherical Variogram Model — varsph.fun
text: x numeric vector non-negative lag distances. nug nugget: semivariance zero lag distance (intercept). psill partial sill: difference sill (total variance) nugget. range range parameter: lag distance sill reached spatial autocorrelation ceases. Beyond distance semivariance constant nug + psill.

title: Spherical Variogram Model — varsph.fun
text: varsph.fun() SSvarsph() return numeric value, DRCvarsph() returns list containing nonlinear function self starter function.

title: Spherical Variogram Model — varsph.fun
text: model defined : $$y = \begin{cases}   \text{nug} + \text{psill}     \left(\frac{3}{2}\frac{x}{\text{range}} -           \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x}{\text{range}}\right)^3\right)     & x \leq \text{range} \\   \text{nug} + \text{psill} & x > \text{range} \end{cases}$$ nug nugget, psill partial sill, range lag distance sill reached exactly. Unlike exponential Gaussian models, spherical model reaches sill finite distance. Unlike exponential Gaussian models, spherical model reaches sill exactly finite distance (range), making suitable hard limit spatial dependence expected.
